item.title: Madang PEB forms El Nino sub committee
item.description: The Madang Provincial Education Board (PEB) has formed a 7th sub- committee for purposes of coordinating El Nino relief efforts in all schools in the province from Early Childhood to Primary, High, Secondary through to Technical Vocational Education Training or TVET institutions. The El Nino Subcommittee was sanctioned by the Secretary for Education, Dr. Uke Kombra.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Education Board (PEB) has formed a 7th sub- committee for purposes of coordinating El Nino relief efforts in all schools in the province from Early Childhood to Primary, High, Secondary through to Technical Vocational Education Training or TVET institutions.

The El Nino Subcommittee was sanctioned by the Secretary for Education, Dr. Uke Kombra.

All provinces in the country are required to have this sub- committee.

In Madang Province, Provincial Administrator Daniel Aloi has also requested the same to be formed by the PEB.

The sub- committee comprises 10 members of the Madang Provincial Education Board, headed and by Rodney Selarn.

This sub- committee is tasked to put together a technical team which will coordinate with District Education Authorities, Church Agencies, school inspectors, school administrators, and school emergency committees to provide data for every level of school.

The data collected will be on water situation, food situation, daily attendance to class by students, teachers conditions at schools, health and sanitation issues, additional information on unforeseen consequences of El Nino.

The data will be captured and recorded by the technical team, overseen by the El Nino sub- committee, and will verify the information and present it to the Office of the Madang Provincial Administrator.

The Office of the Provincial Administrator, which is working in close consultation with the Office of the Madang Governor, will then use the data to engage technical officers and strategic stakeholders to provide appropriate assistance.

The focus of assistance will mainly be on water access and possibly provision of food.

Schools can access the templates for data entry from the technical team at the office of the Madang Provincial Education Board through its executive officer.

item.title: Education Department commits to Kaki secondary and Kopen national school of excellence
item.description: The Ministry for Education committed a sum of one million kina to the Kaki Secondary. During Kaki Secondary School in Enga’s second graduation for grade 10s and first for the pioneer grade 12s of the school last week, Education Minister, Francis Kikin Siune committed a sum of K1million to the school to help in its development.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry for Education committed a sum of one million kina to the Kaki Secondary.

During Kaki Secondary School in Enga’s second graduation for grade 10s and first for the pioneer grade 12s of the school last week, Education Minister, Francis Kikin Siune committed a sum of K1million to the school to help in its development.

While, honoring previous commitment by the education department to the Kopen National School of Excellence worth K5 million.

Clarifying the education Ministers commitment Education Secretary, Dr. Uke Kombra said the K1million is only a commitment made by the education department to Kaki Secondary.

Through the previous Minister, Lucas Dawa Dekena made a commitment to build Kopen an auditorium and a STEM lab, honoring that commitment a K5 Million Kina has been allocated and is available for the Kopen National School of Excellence.

One million Kina to build the STEM lab has already been deposited into the schools account while the four million for the auditorium is available and in the education department’s trust and will be signed over after necessary signings with provincial authorities of Enga.

item.title: DWU students challenged to be leaders of character and purpose
item.description: Final year students at the Divine Word University in Madang have been challenged to become leaders of character and purpose after university life. They were also told that Papua New Guinea needs leaders to lead it, not just brilliant leaders but people who can think with their hearts.
item.content:encoded:
Final year students at the Divine Word University in Madang have been challenged to become leaders of character and purpose after university life.

They were also told that Papua New Guinea needs leaders to lead it, not just brilliant leaders but people who can think with their hearts.

The challenge came from David Kitchnoge, the Chief Investment Officer with Kumuls Consolidated Holdings, whilst delivering the keynote address during Friday's missioning ceremony at the university's SVD Auditorium.

The missioning ceremony, held annually for final year students before they sit for their final examinations; was the 18th for DWU.

Mr Kitchnoge reminded the final year students that serving their calling with humility, obedience, respect, and a spirit of service would bring them rewards far beyond personal success.

He further advised them that employers are nowadays seeking individuals with the right attitude and strong values.

"Employers today are seeking people with the right attitude, organisations are looking for trustworthy counterparties, and the country is crying out for its sons and daughters to lead it with both their hearts and minds," he said.

On behalf of the DWU community, Maria Huaniangre, Madang’s Port Manager with the National Fisheries Authority and a former student of the university, emphasised the importance of character in professional life.

She told the students, "Your degrees will open doors, but your character will keep them open and determine how far you will go."

Huaniangre stressed that qualities such as integrity, humility, honesty, respect, and teamwork are highly valued just as academic achievements.

"People may forget your grades, but they will always remember your professionalism, your work ethics, and the way you treat other people at work," she said.

Archbishop Douglas Young delivered the homily, reflecting on the significance of the missioning cross, and drew inspiration from the Book of Mathew, recalling how Jesus walked through towns and the synagogues, showing and teaching compassion to people who were harassed and helpless.

Archbishop Young encouraged the students to view the world through the eyes of Christ and respond to the needs of others with empathy and understanding.

He added, "It is the hope and prayer of Divine Word University that the graduates, in a genuine missionary spirit, look upon this broken world, this world of suffering with different eyes, with eyes of heart and compassion, and use the ability, knowledge, skills, and talents gained during their time at the university to genuinely serve people."

Meanwhile, university president Professor Fr. Philip Gibbs, in his welcome remarks; highlighted the significance of the occasion as DWU celebrates 30 years as a university.

"This event is a time of thanksgiving, a time of appreciation, and a time of blessings," he said.

Fr. Gibbs further explained that the missioning crosses presented to students symbolise that blessing and serve as a reminder of their responsibility to serve others.

Fr. Gibbs also quoted the university's first president, Professor Fr. Jan Czuba in the 2011 missioning ceremony stating that, "As we gather to celebrate the journey of the students, we are reminded that the education you receive at DWU is not just about academic achievements but about becoming a person of value."

The cross symbolises the graduates' commitment to carry forward the values instilled in them during their time at Divine Word University, and to serve their communities with compassion, respect and love.

item.title: Globe manufacturing company supports Madang Rugby League grand final
item.description: Madang Rugby League has received some timely assistance from Globe Manufacturing Company as it prepares to host its grand final games tomorrow. The company donated tins of paint to mark the Ron Albert Oval ahead of tomorrow's fixtures.
item.content:encoded:
Madang Rugby League has received some timely assistance from Globe Manufacturing Company as it prepares to host its grand final games tomorrow.

The company donated tins of paint to mark the Ron Albert Oval ahead of tomorrow's fixtures.

The donation was formally presented by Globe Manufacturing General Manager, Darmith Fernando, to Madang Rugby League Administrator, Albert Tobe, at the Ron Albert Oval on Thursday.

Tobe has extended the association's sincere appreciation to the company, stating Madang Rugby League has faced significant challenges in securing sufficient financial support from potential sponsors to host a successful grand final this year.

He said, "Therefore, every contribution, big or small, makes a meaningful difference.

"Support such as this from Globe Manufacturing will go a long way towards helping us prepare a quality venue and, more importantly, revive, strengthen, and develop rugby league in Madang Town and the wider province.

"On behalf of the Madang Rugby League Executives, participating clubs, players, and supporters, we extend our sincere appreciation to Globe Manufacturing for standing with rugby league in Madang.

"Thank you, Globe Manufacturing, for supporting the game and our community."

Tomorrow's grandfinals will see Takara 1 Hawks and 6A Bulldogs battle it out for the 2026 title in the Under 20 Men's Division, whilst in the Open Women’s Division, Madang Sisters will challenge Madang Royals.

In the main game, which is the Senior Men's Division, Madang Royals will face off with Takara 1 Hawks.

The gates will be opened at 9 AM with the first game (Under 20 Men's) expected to start at 11 AM, the women's game is scheduled for 1 PM whilst the Senior Men's grand final will kick off at 3 PM.

Executives are urging everyone to be in their best behavior tomorrow.

item.title: Madang Technical College signs MOU with Ramu NiCo
item.description: A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was inked this week in Madang between Madang Technical College and the Chinese developer of the country's only nickel and cobalt project, Ramu NiCo Management Limited. The MOU paves the way for a working collaboration between the college and the company, especially in the area of specialist training for the students.
item.content:encoded:
A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was inked this week in Madang between Madang Technical College and the Chinese developer of the country's only nickel and cobalt project, Ramu NiCo Management Limited.

The MOU paves the way for a working collaboration between the college and the company, especially in the area of specialist training for the students.

The document, described as significant by the college principal, Marcus Weimeia, marks a milestone achievement for the college.

It was signed by the Deputy Secretary of the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology, Charles Mabia, Vice President of Ramu NiCo, Meng Deyong, who signed on behalf of the Company President, Wang Zhou, and Board Chairman of the College, Norman Gulo.

Mabia signed as a witness of the partnership between Ramu NiCo and Madang Technical College.

According to the company's Human Resource Manager, Jeffers Heptol Teargun, who introduced the purpose of the MOU, the document is a first- of- its- kind that Ramu NiCo has entered into with a learning institution in the country.

The MOU is two-fold. It is a collaboration between the company and the college to introduce new courses, designed mainly for the mining industry, and to provide industrial training for students who graduate from the college.

The new courses will include nickel and cobalt processing technology, a course that is not offered at the college and in the country.

"Under the MOU, the company will bring in instructors from China to teach these courses. We will have Chinese trainers to come and inspect, and also develop some courses. For existing courses that the college is already running, we will put more innovation into them

"For students who perform well and impress us during their industrial attachment, the company will give them permanent jobs.

"A partnership will also be established for the company to sponsor some of the students to do short courses and industrial training in China. Even teachers can go for teachers' exchange programs in China," he said.

Teargun stressed that the MOU will require efforts from all parties concerned, including the national government, provincial government, and LLGs, in terms of collaboration and cooperation.

He further stated that through the project's MOA that is under review with the landowners, a proposal is in place for the establishment of a technical vocational training (TVET) centre at Kurumbukari and one in Basamuk.

These centres will allow the local youth population to get national certificates trainings, levels 1 and 2, as well as help boost the technical human resources in the province and country.

DHERST Deputy Secretary, Mr. Mabia, said the department is already working with the industries to write up training packages that are already through the system.

He added, "DHERST is very keen to see the industry work with colleges to help train our young workforce for the future."

Vice-president Meng, in his remarks, gave a brief background of the company's operations in Madang.

He said that as the company prepares to go into phase 2 of the project, it needs more employees.

"We need more technical employees, so we want to provide Chinese technical training and provide facilities to Madang Technical College. We want to help develop some courses that can help give job opportunities to locals," he said.

Meng also revealed that the company currently employs 1, 300 PNG nationals.

Meanwhile, Board Chairman, Gulo said that the signing of the MOU was more than a formal agreement.

He said, "It is a partnership built on shared vision, mutual respect and a commitment to the future of Madang and Papua New Guinea.

"The MOU represents an opportunity to bridge education and the industries."

item.title: Twenty factory made guns surrendered in Koroba Lake Kopiago district

This event marks the first gun surrender program conducted within the Koroba–Lake Kopiago District and stands as the fifth peace ce
item.content:encoded:
Four communities voluntarily surrendered 20 factory-made firearms, over 50 homemade guns, a hand grenade, and various traditional weapons, including bows and arrows on Wednesday.

​The surrender exercise brought together people from Egele, Yaluba 1, Yaluba 2, and Pupa. This event marks the first gun surrender program conducted within the Koroba–Lake Kopiago District and stands as the fifth peace ceremony of its kind across Hela Province.

​The ceremony was witnessed by Governor Philip Undialu, Koroba–Lake Kopiago MP William Bando, Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu, and Provincial Police Commander Inspector Arau Mairi. They were joined by members police, PNGDF personnel and local community leaders.

​Governor Undialu, who leads the Hela Provincial Gun Surrender Program, commended local ward councillors, leaders, and community members for their joint effort to end years of devastating tribal violence and rebuild community peace.

​"We will continue this program throughout Hela until illegal firearms no longer pose a threat to our communities. These foreign weapons have warped minds, turning brother against brother and destroying our villages. Working together, we will restore Hela Province to a place of safety where people can travel freely and access vital services once again," Governor Undialu said.

​Local MP William Bando emphasized that the Yaluba event signals the beginning of a broader, district-wide disarmament drive, praising the local clans for taking a decisive step toward lasting peace.

​"This marks the beginning of our mission to clear weapons from our district. We urge neighboring communities to prepare, as our team will move village by village until every tribe and clan surrenders their arms. We are doing this for the future of our children and our youth, many of whom have been denied an education due to endless tribal conflict," MP Bando remarked, adding that genuine peace is the essential prerequisite for delivering government infrastructure and social services.

​The Hela Provincial Gun Surrender Program continues its rollout across the district, with neighboring villages in the Pureni community scheduled to surrender their weapons today.

item.title: Hela people surrender guns through God’s conviction
item.description: Decades-long tribal conflicts are finally yielding to an unprecedented wave of voluntary disarmament in Hela Province. Through a powerful combination of spiritual conviction, relentless grassroots advocacy, and targeted local governance, long-standing enemy clans and warring tribes are stepping forward to surrender their illegal firearms, says Hela Governor Philip Undialu.
item.content:encoded:
Decades-long tribal conflicts are finally yielding to an unprecedented wave of voluntary disarmament in Hela Province.

Through a powerful combination of spiritual conviction, relentless grassroots advocacy, and targeted local governance, long-standing enemy clans and warring tribes are stepping forward to surrender their illegal firearms, says Hela Governor Philip Undialu.

He said the initiative marks a critical turning point for Hela Province, long burdened by violence, offering its communities a rare and promising path toward lasting peace and socio-economic recovery.

At the heart of this peace movement is a deep, internal awakening driven by faith and community resilience.

Governor Undialu emphasized that the men choosing to lay down their weapons are doing so not out of external coercion, but through genuine divine conviction.

"After years of continuous bloodshed, former tribal enemies recognized that persistent tribal warfare served only to destroy their families, ruin livelihoods, and rob them of basic freedom. The possession of illegal firearms is like being in slavery — with no freedom, only fear," he said.

Governor Undialu stressed that local church organizations, spearheaded by mothers and women's groups, maintained constant prayer vigils, pleading for an end to the violence. He credited these relentless prayers with touching the hearts of gunmen and paving the way for reconciliation.

"By voluntarily stepping away from armed conflict, former warring tribes are now securing an opportunity to reintegrate into society, live without constant fear of retaliation, and rebuild their communities," he said.

The successful implementation of the Gun Surrender Program reflects an intensive, coordinated effort across multiple tiers of provincial leadership and security forces.

As Chairman of the program, Governor Undialu, alongside Koroba-Lake Kopiago MP and Minister for Immigration and Border Security William Bando, Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu, Election Manager John Tipa, Provincial Police Commander Inspector Arau Mairi, LLG Presidents, and members of the police and defence forces, worked around the clock to ensure the program's success.

Governor Undialu said communities made their work easier by identifying every man involved in tribal fights and known to be in possession of illegal guns — a clear sign of true community ownership of the peace process.

item.title: PMGH children’s cancer ward full
item.description: Port Moresby General Hospital's children's cancer ward is operating at full capacity, with growing numbers of children being diagnosed with cancer needing long-term treatment. And there is an urgent need to expand the ward and establish a centralized adult cancer facility.
item.content:encoded:
Port Moresby General Hospital's children's cancer ward is operating at full capacity, with growing numbers of children being diagnosed with cancer needing long-term treatment.

And there is an urgent need to expand the ward and establish a centralized adult cancer facility.

Director Medical Services at Port Moresby General Hospital Dr. Kone Sobi told NBC News, the children's cancer ward at Pom Gen has a bed capacity of 12, and usually all beds are occupied at all times.

The cancer ward was opened almost six years ago and has had some renovations since, but demand has grown.

“It has a bed capacity of 12, so 12 patients can stay. Usually, all the beds are often full, occupied at all times. They can stay anywhere from a few weeks to several months, up to 12 months simply because they're coming from outside Port Moresby." Dr. Sobi said.

Dr. Sobi explained that children come from outside Port Moresby, from other provinces, for chemotherapy which goes in cycles — once or twice a week every month for up to six months, depending on the cancer type.

Some stay up to 12 months because they cannot return home between treatments.

He said children around Port Moresby are discharged and return for outpatient clinic.

“There is really a need to increase the capacity because of the growing number of children being diagnosed. We are fortunate in pediatrics to have a designated ward for children with cancer, but in adults, they are all spread out. We look forward to a facility that can have inpatients all in one section. "He said.

While children are fortunate to have a designated ward, adult cancers are spread out — women's cancers at obstetrics and gynecology, surgical cancers in surgical wards, and other cancers in internal medicine wards.

On prevention, he said patients come at quite advanced stages and stressed early detection, with robust screening in communities, especially for common cancers in PNG like mouth cancer, breast and cervical cancer in women, and leukemia in children.

item.title: Illegal firearms to be surrendered before December 25
item.description: Minister for Immigration and Border Security and Member for Koroba-Lake Kopiago, William Bando, warned community members holding illegal weapons: "Turn them in before the provincial Gun Surrender Program amnesty expires on December 25, or face severe tactical intervention."
